title: Zurna
summary: The zurna is a loud conical double-reed pipe used outdoors for weddings and village dances, usually with a drum. A wide wooden bell flares from a short body, and a flat disc rests against the lips so the player can breathe in through the nose while the sound continues.
howToPlay: A covered hole glows; an open hole shows its dark bore. Seven notes of the mode are lit down the tube.
Each strike shows the fingering of that note and the bell opens as it sounds.
Keep the notes flowing, the way a dance call does.
rules: A phrase is a line of notes, each struck close to its beat.
Long notes swell slowly: strike on the beat and let them ring.
The round ends when the last note has been judged; the score is the share of the best possible.
heritageNote: The player circular-breathes into the reed and fingers the holes while a davul player keeps the rhythm, so the tune never stops for breath.
credits: Tradition: the zurna; phrases written for this game
